title: Using Rapid-cycle Evaluation to Examine and Justify Edtech Investments
snippet: Discover how LearnPlatform and rapid-cycle evaluations gave Edmonds School
intro: Discover how LearnPlatform and rapid-cycle evaluations gave Edmonds School District the data to know which edtech tools were effective and worthy of renewals.

body.heading: Situation
body.text: The Edmonds School District serves more than 20,000 students just north of Seattle. Like many large districts, Edmonds invested in many edtech tools, but struggled to evaluate whether those tools delivered results. Which tools were being used? And were they positively impacting student achievement? Tracking tool effectiveness proved impossible. And when it came time to decide whether or not to renew high-cost tools, they had no foundation of reliable data to stand on. “All we could do was listen to what the vendor was telling us,” said Chris Bailey, Director of Technology. Vendor reports and gut feelings weren’t enough to justify six-figure renewal decisions. The district needed a clear, internal view of what was being used, what was working, and the relationship between the two.
body.html:
The Edmonds School District serves more than 20,000 students just north of Seattle. Like many large districts, Edmonds invested in many edtech tools, but struggled to evaluate whether those tools delivered results. Which tools were being used? And were they positively impacting student achievement?

Tracking tool effectiveness proved impossible. And when it came time to decide whether or not to renew high-cost tools, they had no foundation of reliable data to stand on. “All we could do was listen to what the vendor was telling us,” said Chris Bailey, Director of Technology.

Vendor reports and gut feelings weren’t enough to justify six-figure renewal decisions. The district needed a clear, internal view of what was being used, what was working, and the relationship between the two.

body.text: We don’t want to commit to a five-year contract without evidence. [With LearnPlatform], we can assess outcomes for ourselves, and the data will tell us whether we should keep going.
body.html:
We don’t want to commit to a five-year contract without evidence. [With LearnPlatform], we can assess outcomes for ourselves, and the data will tell us whether we should keep going.

Chris BaileyDirector of Technology, Edmonds School District, WA

body.heading: Insights
body.text: Working with the LearnPlatform research team, Edmonds began Rapid-cycle Evaluations (RCE), which shifted their thinking. “We started with, ‘Who’s using this?’ Then, ‘Are they using it enough?’” said Bailey. “Eventually, we got to, ‘Are students growing?’ And that’s the question that really mattered.” Through dozens of rapid-cycle evaluations powered by LearnPlatform, district leadership uncovered key insights: Usage ≠ impact: Just because a tool is used frequently doesn’t mean it translates to student growth, prompting deeper analysis of factors like time in the tool or modules completed. Internal data changes conversations: Instead of relying on vendor claims or best guesses, the team could lean on independent data when aligning district leaders, staff, and the school board. “We’ve started asking questions we never thought we could answer,” said Bailey. “And that’s changed the way we think about both new tools and tools we’ve had for years.” “Every time we did a study, we learned more about what was important to the Edmonds team,” said Amanda Cadran, RCE Program Director at LearnPlatform. “And that shaped the next study and the study after that, which is how the process works best.” That iterative mindset changed Edmonds’ approach to evaluation. Instead of static snapshots, every RCE builds on the last, which has helped the district refine what success means and how to measure it.

Working with the LearnPlatform research team, Edmonds began Rapid-cycle Evaluations (RCE), which shifted their thinking. “We started with, ‘Who’s using this?’ Then, ‘Are they using it enough?’” said Bailey. “Eventually, we got to, ‘Are students growing?’ And that’s the question that really mattered.”

Through dozens of rapid-cycle evaluations powered by LearnPlatform, district leadership uncovered key insights:

  • Usage ≠ impact: Just because a tool is used frequently doesn’t mean it translates to student growth, prompting deeper analysis of factors like time in the tool or modules completed.
  • Internal data changes conversations: Instead of relying on vendor claims or best guesses, the team could lean on independent data when aligning district leaders, staff, and the school board.

“We’ve started asking questions we never thought we could answer,” said Bailey. “And that’s changed the way we think about both new tools and tools we’ve had for years.”

“Every time we did a study, we learned more about what was important to the Edmonds team,” said Amanda Cadran, RCE Program Director at LearnPlatform. “And that shaped the next study and the study after that, which is how the process works best.”

That iterative mindset changed Edmonds’ approach to evaluation. Instead of static snapshots, every RCE builds on the last, which has helped the district refine what success means and how to measure it.

body.heading: Solution
body.text: Edmonds built a repeatable, data-driven evaluation model with LearnPlatform at the center. First, they streamlined tool requests and approvals, replacing Google Forms and spreadsheets with a centralized system. With real-time visibility, they shifted to rapid- cycle evaluation to go beyond usage to the impact of edtech tools. In partnership with the LearnPlatform research team at Instructure, they looked at engagement and fidelity patterns across grade bands and time. That work led to a validated research design, which allowed them to connect student outcomes to usage fidelity. This level of analysis aligned with Edmonds’ goal to inform implementation and renewal strategies and only happened because the district committed to iteration.

title: University of North Texas | Case Study
snippet: First-of-its-kind learner record empowers UNT students to build marketable
intro: First-of-its-kind learner record empowers UNT students to build marketable skills portfolio

body.text: Since 2016, the University of North Texas has helped students develop the marketable skills that can give them an edge in the job market. But over time, UNT discovered that enabling students to build skills wasn’t enough. Without a way to visualize those skills, many students didn’t fully understand them—and struggled to communicate them to potential employers. A groundbreaking new partnership between UNT’s Career Connect program and Parchment Digital Badges is tackling that problem. UNT rolled out a Parchment Digital Badgesbased Comprehensive Learner Record (CLR), a verifiable digital record that collects marketable skills in the form of badges and credentials. Capturing what’s missing from the traditional academic transcript, the Learner Record helps students visualize and better understand the skills they’ve developed and makes it easy for students to share them with the outside world. “By prompting, suggesting structure, and providing opportunities for students to collect and connect their experiences, we have a better chance of supporting their success,” explained Mike Simmons, Assistant Vice President for Academic Affairs at UNT. “Students have a random collection of experiences that can be represented by digital badges, but the organizing and articulation of experiences in which badges add up to a credential seems to us to be the trick. The sooner in their academic experience that they do that, the better!”

body.heading: Personal responsibility
body.text: “UNT’s Learner Record was developed in collaboration with students to fit seamlessly into the Parchment Digital Badges badging platform, and it is now available to any organization.” Simmons said, “We selected the [Parchment Digital Badges] platform because of its use and promotion of open standards such as badges,” which are embedded with secure data that verifies badge origin, authenticity, and the specific learning and skills represented. “Parchment Digital Badges seamless integration with Canvas LMS is also very helpful.” The Parchment Digital Badges Learner Record is designed for interoperability and incorporates all eight characteristics identified by IMS Global, one of the organizations working to define open standards for CLRs.

body.heading: Transitioning to badging
body.text: Marketable skills — also called 21st century skills or soft skills — refer to real-world competencies such as communication, critical thinking, teamwork, and leadership. Employers value these in prospective employees but often can’t identify them in recent college graduates. Learn more about how virtual learning is enabling lifelong skills building here . Career Connect bridges this skills gap and helps students become more career ready as they move into the workforce. Like many universities and higher education institutions, UNT offers High-Impact Practices (HIPs) to support student learning and retention. In coursework and in experiences outside the classroom, HIPs such as internships, service learning, and capstones help students build and demonstrate key marketable skills. Rather than treating digital badges simply as something to be earned going forward, UNT decided to issue badges to thousands of students for learning that happened in prior semesters. This program is working as designed: early evidence points to positive impacts on student persistence and outcomes. But UNT realized it could do more to help graduates land jobs. Simmons explained that because UNT structured the Career Connect assessment process similarly to the concept of badging — that is, students submit evidence to earn awards that articulate their learning achievements — transitioning the program to digital badge– based learning pathways was relatively straightforward.

body.heading: How to earn a UNT-awarded skill credential
body.text: Now, students begin the journey toward each full credential by earning digital badges for experiences. For example, when students complete a special assignment in a French Debate course or a community advocacy project in a Communications Studies class, they can earn a badge that represents demonstrated critical thinking. Students accumulate, or stack, badges in different ways to earn an Essential Knowledge Micro-credential and a Demonstrated Proficiency Micro-credential, with work assessed individually at each stage. Once a student earns both microcredentials, UNT awards the full credential for that skill.

body.text: In addition to the credentials that demonstrate intercurricular competencies gained from a variety of experiences, UNT students can pursue credentials that demonstrate marketable skills in the context of their major — a novel offering in higher education. For example, a student pursuing the French B.A. Marketable Skills credential might demonstrate critical thinking and empirical analysis by engaging in a course-based debate experience. That has obvious value in the job market, but it has value to the students as well, who can better understand how their curriculum-based work is developing real-world skills. It helps them make connections to a broader skill set they might otherwise overlook when reading a syllabus and course requirements. Meena Naik, Program Director of Career Connect, explained, “These credential stacks are not mutually inclusive and they are designed to play off one another. Badges can serve multiple purposes, and they count in multiple sets of credentials, or pathways, as we organize competency stacks in different ways." "For example, when a student in a French course does a project activity that demonstrates teamwork or critical thinking that is specific to that course in curriculum, it also applies to the broader accumulation of their teamwork and critical thinking skills in the university-wide, interdisciplinary marketable skills credential.”

Meena Naik, Program Director of Career Connect, explained, “These credential stacks are not mutually inclusive and they are designed to play off one another. Badges can serve multiple purposes, and they count in multiple sets of credentials, or pathways, as we organize competency stacks in different ways."

"For example, when a student in a French course does a project activity that demonstrates teamwork or critical thinking that is specific to that course in curriculum, it also applies to the broader accumulation of their teamwork and critical thinking skills in the university-wide, interdisciplinary marketable skills credential.”

body.heading: Visualizing Success
body.text: When UNT students log in, a unique Parchment Digital Badges dashboard feature visualizes for them, in real time, the UNT badges, micro-credentials, and credentials that are completed and in progress. This unique representation of their work helps them understand their learning journey in a meaningful context, identify opportunities, and make decisions about what to pursue next. Students determine which progress to include in the Learner Record, how to organize it, and whether to make it public or private. Consumers of the records, such as potential employers, not only get an overview of the work, but can click on any badge or credential to see details about the work it represents, how the skill was assessed, and which pathway the learner took to earn it. Parchment Digital Badges includes pathways that display the learning journey required to earn a credential, including different options for fulfilling requirements. Parchment Digital Badges’ powerful analytics allow university administrators to monitor how students are progressing through their Career Connect work, track how they’re sharing their work on social media, and measure program outcomes.

title: Joni and Friends expands global access to inclusive learning with Canvas
snippet: Joni and Friends uses Canvas to scale accessible, tech-powered learning
intro: Joni and Friends uses Canvas to scale accessible, tech-powered learning—empowering global nonprofit training with inclusive tools that just work.

body.text: Joni and Friends, an international disability ministry, is dedicated to transforming the lives of people with disabilities through programs that offer practical help and spiritual hope to people living with disability. With international outreaches, domestic Family Retreats, and an expanding portfolio of training programs for volunteers, students, and faith leaderss, the organization needed a platform to centralize, scale, and deliver instruction that meets the needs of every learner, regardless of ability or location.
body.html: Joni and Friends, an international disability ministry, is dedicated to transforming the lives of people with disabilities through programs that offer practical help and spiritual hope to people living with disability. With international outreaches, domestic Family Retreats, and an expanding portfolio of training programs for volunteers, students, and faith leaderss, the organization needed a platform to centralize, scale, and deliver instruction that meets the needs of every learner, regardless of ability or location.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: Joni and Friends had outgrown its legacy learning tools. Their previous platform simply couldn’t keep up with the needs of a multifaceted operation managing everything from semester-long internships and Family Retreat staff training to global disability ministry courses. The lack of automation and integration made it increasingly difficult to deliver consistent, high-quality training across audiences. “Our team is small, and our impact is big,” said Aimée Stork, Senior Manager of Online Education. “We were managing training for volunteers, staff, interns, and members of the public—often manually—and it just wasn’t sustainable.” The team needed an LMS that was both robust and intuitive, capable of handling multilingual content, rich accessibility requirements, and diverse learner paths. Above all, it had to align with their mission of dignity and belonging for all.

title: UTampa Prepares for a Bright Future With Canvas
snippet: At the University of Tampa, a new curriculum and doubling enrollment called for
intro: At the University of Tampa, a new curriculum and doubling enrollment called for a new LMS.

media.transcript: My name is Jenna Lash. I am the director in ITS Academic Solutions. UTampo's culture is amazing. The university has a lot of history with Plant Hall, our original building on campus, and that now being such a staple when you think of Tampa as a city in general. We've grown so much. When I started here, our entire enrollment was around fifteen hundred, and our incoming classes are now about three thousand. Our students come from all over the country really in search of an experience that is personalized, that is engaging. One of the things we're really focused on strategically is improving graduation rates. We've been on our previous LMS for twenty one years, and technology does at one point become outdated. We've had Spartan Studies launching. Spartan Studies is our core curriculum here at the university that every undergraduate student goes through. Milestones that they hit and certain assignments that they turn in that we then pull for assessment. Rolling out a new core curriculum and a new learning management system at the same time can be daunting. It's all started with having faculty be part of the selection process. I've used a few different LMSs before. One of the things that I really liked about the transition to Canvas, I've done it a few times at different schools, and it's always very easy, very seamless. Canvas has made creating excellent course content much easier. Canvas being in the cloud and being able to seamlessly integrate with other applications is really important for us. Many faculty were very excited. Faculty, staff, students, very excited to be moving over to Canvas. I would have them say, when are we getting Canvas? When are we getting Canvas? I really like Canvas because of the ways that you can personalize. One of them is changing the color on your dashboard. So I can make all my assignments different colors and organize it that way. Mostly, I use it for my assignments and my homeworks and to give an exam. That was also new to me, like, giving an exam on an application. That was so easy. Here at the University of Tampa was my first time ever using Canvas. Before then, I used Schoology, Google Classroom, and I'd say Canvas definitely is the best platform to stay organized with my classes. It makes me see the announcements. It, I have all my homeworks over there. I can keep a record of everything. So it is like a bridge between the teacher and the student, and it is it has helped us a lot. It's useful to have the app in addition to having it on my computer. It helps me stay engaged with my classmates, people who have profile pictures. I get the notifications right on my phone when things are graded or when things are assigned, so I always have access to my assignments and my grades. I've really enjoyed using Canvas, specifically the mobile Canvas. Feedback comes in the form of, I read your message that you wrote in the margins, and I was really confused, confused, but then you have the audio feedback. So that was really helpful. So I think so far students have really enjoyed having that. The fact that Canvas can provide real time analytics and a lot of data to understand how students are engaging with courses is incredibly helpful. Utilizing the technology and what it has in it allows us to focus on really being able to to work with our students and help our students learn and grow. It has been a huge, huge tool for us in the college that would really help to enhance the teaching and learning in the classroom and the student experience and engagement, and hopefully overall student success and graduation rates as well. I think it is so important to be a lifelong learner, and I just wanted to keep learning as long as I can. And even after I graduate college, I'm gonna continue learning. I've been a student for, like, twenty five years of my life now, and throughout my life, I plan to learn many more skills that will help me grow as a man. What I enjoy most about the work that I do is making a difference in people's lives.

title: TEL Education + Canvas: Delivering Mission-Driven Learning at Scale
snippet: TEL Education uses Canvas to scale dual enrollment, boost pass rates by 12%, and
intro: TEL Education uses Canvas to scale dual enrollment, boost pass rates by 12%, and deliver accessible, mission-driven learning to 7,000+ students.

body.text: TEL Education is a nonprofit committed to making college more affordable and accessible, especially for students from underserved backgrounds. By offering scalable, online general education courses, TEL builds bridges between high schools and universities, helping students earn college credit while still in high school. Through its turnkey dual enrollment program—which includes a high school partnerships team, curriculum and instruction experts, and dedicated support staff—TEL now serves institutions such as McMurry University, Oklahoma Christian University, Mid-America Christian University, Briar Cliff University, Warner Pacific University, Cedar Crest College, and Andrew College. As enrollments doubled, TEL partnered with Canvas to streamline delivery and improve the learning experience.
body.html:
TEL Education is a nonprofit committed to making college more affordable and accessible, especially for students from underserved backgrounds. By offering scalable, online general education courses, TEL builds bridges between high schools and universities, helping students earn college credit while still in high school.

Through its turnkey dual enrollment program—which includes a high school partnerships team, curriculum and instruction experts, and dedicated support staff—TEL now serves institutions such as McMurry University, Oklahoma Christian University, Mid-America Christian University, Briar Cliff University, Warner Pacific University, Cedar Crest College, and Andrew College. As enrollments doubled, TEL partnered with Canvas to streamline delivery and improve the learning experience.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: TEL Education's legacy learning platform was built for a much smaller operation. As the organization grew rapidly, with enrollments jumping from 1,500 to nearly 7,000 per semester, the increased demand outpaced the capabilities of the existing infrastructure. Instructors had limited communication tools, essential course updates were cumbersome, and reporting lacked the depth needed to track student performance or inform improvements. Though their previous system provided a foundation, there was an opportunity to enhance the system’s accessibility and improve the overall experience for students. TEL's mission depends on affordability and access; their technology had become a barrier to both. They needed a robust, flexible platform that could scale quickly and support personalized instruction at a high volume.

body.heading: Key Insights
body.text: User-friendly design is critical for TEL's underserved, first-gen students to stay engaged and succeed in online learning. Canvas' flexible tools and APIs helped TEL scale fast while keeping courses consistent and easy to manage. Strong instructor-student interaction in Canvas led to higher engagement and a 12% boost in student pass rates. Canvas Trust integration lets students access TEL courses through partner schools, strengthening collaboration.

  • Canvas' flexible tools and APIs helped TEL scale fast while keeping courses consistent and easy to manage.
  • Strong instructor-student interaction in Canvas led to higher engagement and a 12% boost in student pass rates.
  • Canvas Trust integration lets students access TEL courses through partner schools, strengthening collaboration.

body.heading: The Solution
body.text: To support rapid growth and deliver a better learning experience, TEL Education transitioned to Canvas. Instructors gained access to SpeedGrader and messaging tools, enabling timely, personalized feedback—something the previous platform couldn't offer. Canvas' sub-account and sectioning features allowed TEL to efficiently manage multiple partner schools and terms while reusable templates supported consistent, scalable course design. TEL's instructional team created rich, interactive content using custom HTML and CSS without needing external design tools. Integrations with Copyleaks and Honorlock reinforced academic integrity, and Canvas APIs enabled custom reporting for continuous improvement. With Canvas, TEL didn't just upgrade its technology—they built a flexible foundation for meaningful, mission-driven learning at scale.

Dr. Michele HaynesVice President, Academics, TEL Education

body.heading: Built For Scale, Designed For Impact
body.text: Canvas has allowed TEL Education to reimagine what effective, accessible, and engaging online education can look like—without requiring a massive development team or third-party design tools. Their instructional designers, many early in their careers, are building highly interactive, visually compelling courses using just HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. This scrappy, creative approach has resulted in courses that rival professionally designed content—and instructors now regularly embed videos, host discussions, and provide annotated feedback with ease. Beyond content delivery, Canvas supports internal operations. TEL has developed a central Instructional Support Hub for onboarding and compliance, managing everything from cybersecurity training to FERPA certification. With Canvas as both a student- and staff- facing platform, TEL has streamlined operations and strengthened organizational cohesion.

body.heading: Building Trust Through Shared Technology
body.text: In a model built on partnerships between high schools and universities, cohesion across systems matters. TEL Education leverages Canvas Trust relationships to deepen its collaboration with institutions like McMurry University. These partnerships allow students enrolled at TEL to access their courses directly through their home institution's Canvas instance. This means a seamless experience for students—no need to navigate multiple platforms or logins. For institutional partners, it creates alignment and continuity, reinforcing the credibility and integration of TEL's programs. TEL's ability to meet partners where they are, both technically and pedagogically, has become a key differentiator. "The move to Canvas enabled our campus to deliver quality and consistent instruction at scale. As our Dual Credit program grew from 20 students to nearly 2,000 students the homegrown LMS taxed our staff by requiring quite extensive manual intervention for administrative tasks like course enrollment. Additionally, our DCA program requires our university to integrate seamlessly with TEL Education to share resources and information," shared Dr. Grant Greenwood, McMurry University. "Canvas provided an opportunity to unify our separate LMS instances (TEL Education's instance and McMurry University's instance) through a bridge that reduced student confusion on how to navigate the LMS and improved the user experience. Moving fully to Canvas has enabled our teams to focus on education and service rather than IT and LMS support."

intro: Located in Augusta, Georgia, on the border with South Carolina, Richmond County Schools is a district of over 30,000 students and 4,000 staff, 2,000 of which are classroom teachers. With the help of Impact by Instructure, they successfully onboarded students, parents, and teachers to their learning management system, Canvas.

With the help of Impact by Instructure , they successfully onboarded students, parents, and teachers to their learning management system, Canvas .
body.html: Located in Augusta, Georgia, on the border with South Carolina, Richmond County Schools is a district of over 30,000 students and 4,000 staff, 2,000 of which are classroom teachers. With the help of Impact by Instructure, they successfully onboarded students, parents, and teachers to their learning management system, Canvas.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: In 2020, Richmond County faced the challenge of virtually implementing a new learning management system for all 58 of its schools. In a matter of weeks, they would need to train and onboard their entire learning community. “We had six schools from the pilot that had heard of Canvas before,” Kim Stripling, Program Specialist for the district, said. “Everyone else was new.” Adopting a new learning management system that genuinely improves student outcomes requires collaboration, strategy, and clear communication. The long-term goal was for every user at Richmond County to feel confident engaging with Canvas to support innovative learning strategies in their classrooms. They also needed to consolidate all of their digital learning materials. Stripling described their curriculum and other learning materials before Canvas as “scattered all over the place between Dropbox and Google Drives.” When Richmond County returned to the classroom after remote learning, some teachers were hesitant to continue embracing the new environment. Identifying these teachers and finding avenues to support them has been critical to their success and made more accessible with Impact by Instructure.

They also needed to consolidate all of their digital learning materials. Stripling described their curriculum and other learning materials before Canvas as “scattered all over the place between Dropbox and Google Drives.”

When Richmond County returned to the classroom after remote learning, some teachers were hesitant to continue embracing the new environment. Identifying these teachers and finding avenues to support them has been critical to their success and made more accessible with Impact by Instructure.

body.heading: Key Insights
body.text: Richmond County successfully rolled out Canvas LMS virtually to all 58 schools with strategic professional development and support from Impact by Instructure. Impact by Instructure is simple to implement and quickly allows district-level personnel to see which teachers are or aren’t adopting features in Canvas LMS. Hiring Instructure’s Principal Learning Consultants helped Richmond County plan, guide, and strategize efficiently. Using Canvas LMS and Impact together has allowed Richmond County to increase educator engagement and improve student outcomes.

body.heading: The Solution
body.text: Canvas LMS served as their one-stop digital shop that housed their curriculum, learning materials, and even courses for teacher professional development. Impact by Instructure–through its targeted, in-app messaging–empowered them to encourage everyone to engage deeply with Canvas LMS and implement high-quality instructional strategies . ”Our implementation of Impact was remarkably painless… Compared to some of the other things we’ve implemented, it was one of the easiest…The level of support we received from the Instructure team has been phenomenal,” Dr. Owen Fletcher, Digital Learning Coordinator, said.

Kim StriplingProgram Specialist

body.heading: Accessible, Actionable Data
body.text: Schools usually turn to data to evaluate the implementation and adoption of a new Edtech tool. Curating and responding to this data takes time and effort. Fletcher explained their process for diving into the data and how Impact enabled them to identify usage patterns. “You have to be careful when looking at a pile of data. Earlier this week, I looked at the tools used in the past month. We have a pretty good adoption rate of Discussions in Canvas LMS. I saw that student responses are about half the rate of teachers using the tools. At first glance, it looked good, but then I realized we needed to do some work to get students to respond. That would have been impossible to spot without Impact,” Fletcher said. Upon recognizing this crucial need, Fletcher and the Richmond County team have created targeted professional development to support deeper usage of key features like Discussions. Fletcher has continued to turn to Impact to help design transformative support solutions that meet teachers where they are. “With Impact, we’re now much more proactive instead of reactive. We can set up campaigns ahead of time to support teachers. For example, we ran a digital citizenship campaign at the beginning of the school year. Upon login to Canvas, teachers see a message that gives them the required resources to share with students,” Fletcher said.

body.text: General Assembly (GA), a part of The Adecco Group, is dedicated to empowering individuals and organizations through high-quality education and training. Since 2011, they have helped over 110,000 alumni launch tech careers while supporting top companies in building diverse, scalable talent pipelines. As they grew, challenges with their existing learning infrastructure began to surface, prompting them to seek a more efficient and scalable solution to enhance learning delivery and student recognition.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: Before adopting Canvas LMS in 2019, the state department grappled with outdated training delivery methods. title: Union Public Schools: How Intelligent Insights Powers Data Personalization

intro: Union Public Schools is a standalone community not too far from Tulsa and Broken Arrow, Oklahoma. It’s on a mission to “graduate 100 percent of our students, college and career ready.”

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: Gart Morris serves as the Director of Instructional Technology at Union Public Schools. He has over 20 years of experience at the district across a wide range of roles–principal, assistant principal, and now director of technology. Because of his experience, he deeply understands the type of data administrators need to make informed decisions for faculty and students. He describes his current role as overseeing” how we use technology in the classroom between teachers, administrators, and students.” “We needed to make some strong moves into student technology,” Morris explained. “We didn't have an LMS, but we were at that point where it would be necessary. So the superintendent asked me to take on the role of director of instructional technology and oversee bringing Canvas to our district.” Their district has been using Canvas LMS since 2016 when they piloted it to their ninth-grade class. “We have expanded it grade level by grade level each year. We are now using Canvas as our only grade book in secondary. We were syncing grades to Infinite Campus for a couple of years, and I realized there was no benefit to it. Switching to Canvas as our grade book made my teachers very happy.” A vital part of Morris’s role is tracking data and ensuring that everyone in the district–from teachers to administrators—has access to the information they need to do their jobs well. “My priority was to guarantee that our principals could access reports and data smoothly. This includes percentages on how many students are failing, the number of missing assignments, and failing grades in each class. Within a K-12 environment, administrators need to review these factors quickly to evaluate our teaching staff effectively,” he explained. ”When administrators request specific information, sometimes, this involves me manually exporting CSV files from Canvas LMS as thoroughly to create my own data sets.” Creating these data sets is an essential but often manual process.

intro: Learn how Calcasieu Parish School Board partners with Canvas LMS to simplify teachers' daily workflows and improve students' college readiness.

body.text: Calcasieu Parish School Board (CPSB) is made up of 60 sites that serve children. Under the leadership of their technology facilitation team, the district has implemented a comprehensive approach to technology integration that emphasizes the purposeful use of tools–such as an LMS–to support consistent curriculum and instruction. Teachers, admin, and faculty are united in their mission of “building foundations for the future.”

Under the leadership of their technology facilitation team, the district has implemented a comprehensive approach to technology integration that emphasizes the purposeful use of tools–such as an LMS–to support consistent curriculum and instruction. Teachers, admin, and faculty are united in their mission of “building foundations for the future.”

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: CPSB, like many other districts, wants to ensure that all students regardless of which school they attend or which teachers they have, received a consistent, high-quality educational experience. Technology can play a powerful role in accomplishing that mission. However, teachers found themselves juggling multiple edtech tools. After COVID and hurricane-related closures, the district realized that the previous learning management system needed to be re-evaluated. A committee of stakeholders evaluated multiple tools and determined that Canvas would be a good fit. "Transitioning to Canvas was the right move, even though it felt a little overwhelming at first," said Anissa Fontenot, Technology Facilitator at the district. Calcasieu Parish set out to provide flexible, personalized support that meets educators where they were and roll out a more robust learning management system.

media.transcript: My name is Selena Pellet, and I've gone from a professional dancer to an award winning dairy farmer. The first career that I chose was to be a professional dancer. Went through rehab and we, as a family, moved out to the Gloucester region. The dairy farm had a couple of jobs going and I was getting very excited about learning more and more about the industry. And so from there, they were able to offer me a traineeship, which is where I then started to attend Tocal Agricultural College. We were then introduced to Canvas. It made life a lot simpler. It was very straightforward. We were able to just log on in the first thing in the morning, see what we needed to do throughout the day, and then build on that throughout the week while we were here. So coming from a non agricultural background, the use of Canvas helped me to kind of set where I want to go in life and grow and prosper and look up into the future and help bring dairy farming to life.

body.heading: The Value Of Evidence
body.text: Instructure and ChalkTalk share a vision of how evidence transforms the edtech landscape. “We’re moving away from where research has to be done in multi-year cycles to a place where a teacher can try an intervention, see how effective it was, and try another strategy either in that class or the next one. We’re really reducing the iteration time here– the feedback loop to teachers and educators on efficiency– from decades to days,” Vaisman shared. Some of the studies Instructure’s team has completed for ChalkTalk consider metrics like graduation rates and high-stakes test score improvement compared to the national average. In targeted populations where ChalkTalk helps with students’ graduation requirements, the company was able to determine their impact in helping thousands of students graduate. title: University of Tampa: Rolling out New Curriculum and Canvas LMS Together
snippet: Learn how UTampa embraced new curriculum with Canvas LMS
intro: Learn how UTampa embraced new curriculum with Canvas LMS

body.text: Located in the heart of downtown Tampa, Florida, The University of Tampa (UTampa) is a private university that serves a diverse and dynamic learning community across four colleges. After 20+ years of using Blackboard Learn as its learning management system (LMS), Blackboard announced in Fall 2021 that future efforts would be concentrated on another platform. Enhancements and bug fixes would no longer be made to Blackboard Learn, the platform that housed all of UTampa’s courses at the time. With these changes, UTampa would need to complete a full course migration to Blackboard Learn Ultra, Blackboard’s newer module-based LMS, which was equivalent to the process of migrating to a new LMS. Recognizing the drastic changes that had taken place in the LMS market, UTampa saw this as an opportunity to explore other LMS solutions that would better suit its cloud-first strategy and growing course needs.
body.html:
Located in the heart of downtown Tampa, Florida, The University of Tampa (UTampa) is a private university that serves a diverse and dynamic learning community across four colleges. After 20+ years of using Blackboard Learn as its learning management system (LMS), Blackboard announced in Fall 2021 that future efforts would be concentrated on another platform. Enhancements and bug fixes would no longer be made to Blackboard Learn, the platform that housed all of UTampa’s courses at the time.

With these changes, UTampa would need to complete a full course migration to Blackboard Learn Ultra, Blackboard’s newer module-based LMS, which was equivalent to the process of migrating to a new LMS. Recognizing the drastic changes that had taken place in the LMS market, UTampa saw this as an opportunity to explore other LMS solutions that would better suit its cloud-first strategy and growing course needs.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: In response to the pandemic, UTampa began rapidly developing online courses and in Fall 2020 its Faculty Senate approved a new core curriculum, Spartan Studies. The timing of this newly-approved curriculum presented a unique opportunity. Changing to a new LMS while rolling out new curriculum and courses would allow UTampa’s faculty to build courses within a new system, instead of creating courses in Blackboard Learn that would eventually need to be moved to a new LMS. By selecting an LMS that could be live by Fall 2023, UTampa could combine two of the university’s largest efforts.

body.heading: The Solution
body.text: In 2022, under the support and guidance of Tammy Loper, Vice President of Information Technology and Security, created SpartanLearn, an initiative to select an effective LMS. The new system would need to meet the diverse needs of faculty and students, providing features and capabilities that support a positive experience with technology and courses that are engaging and accessible. From the initiative and collaborative efforts across campus, the SpartanLearn Committee was established to select an LMS with an intuitive, user-friendly interface and rich toolset that delivers innovative course delivery for students. Feedback from faculty, staff, and students was of utmost importance in the selection process, as well as data-driven analytics, data security and accessibility evaluations, LMS market research, and rigorous testing of integration capabilities. In the end, the SpartanLearn Committee recommended Canvas to executive leaders for approval and adoption.

Tammy LoperVice President of Information Technology and Security (ITS), University of Tampa

body.heading: Backed by Faculty
body.text: The SpartanLearn Committee knew that their LMS recommendation to Academic Leadership had to be backed by faculty and the committee saw the vendor demonstrations as a way to involve more faculty in the early decision-making. Vendors from both Canvas and Blackboard Ultra were invited to campus for a three-day vendor demonstration in which the vendors hosted separate sessions for faculty and students. To garner as much participation as possible, the committee created the SpartanLearn website to post the vendor demonstration schedule, provided letters to faculty from the Provost regarding the committee’s vision and goals, and to share opportunities for involvement. Faculty were given the opportunity to sign-up for access to the sandbox demo courses, demo day recordings, and LMS post-demo feedback surveys. Feedback from the surveys were collected over the course of several weeks, with the preferred LMS choice being clear. Comparing the Canvas and Ultra responses, the committee found that 86% of Canvas survey respondents recommended the adoption of Canvas. Alternatively, only 24% of respondents on the Blackboard Ultra survey recommended its adoption. The survey responses revealed that faculty and students strongly preferred the adoption of Canvas, which was further supported by the feature rankings that were much more favorable to the features of Canvas than to Ultra. Survey feedback led a large majority of the committee to vote in favor of Canvas, and UTampa’s Academic Leadership approved the selection of Canvas in January of 2023.

body.heading: Support for All Involved
body.text: Having a new centrally-located technology building built on campus presented UTampa with a timely opportunity to offer in-person training sessions and migration workshops. Numerous in-person, hybrid, and Zoom training sessions, workshops, and 1:1 assistance were made available to faculty to make the transition as seamless as possible. To help faculty be fully prepared for launch, the Academic Solutions team held drop-in sessions and office hours, provided self-service and on-demand opportunities, and created a dedicated course – one for faculty and one for students – to help develop Canvas skills. The team held Canvas Coaching Sessions at the start of the term to assist faculty with all of their questions. More than 40 faculty attended those drop-in sessions. To avoid building from scratch and to augment faculty training offerings, Information Technology and Security at UTampa leveraged resources already available, including the Canvas Faculty Training Course, Instructor Guide, consulting hours for Canvas Coaching sessions, and video training series. Over 145 faculty members also self-enrolled in online courses that the Academic Solutions team offered. “To see so many of our faculty self-enroll into that course was fantastic,” Lash said. “We invited Pearson, McGraw-Hill, and Cengage, our top three incorporated publishers because we receive numerous incidents that we can’t fully assist with since our team doesn’t have administrative access,” Lash said. “We also set up Zoom sessions with the publisher and a faculty member, facilitating troubleshooting meetings as needed.” Resources and training are offered for students through UTampa’s Advanced Digital Literacy Center. Additionally, there is an online course available to students seeking Canvas support, to ensure everyone at UTampa has access to the support they need.

intro: Discover how Generation: You Employed leverages Canvas LMS to provide effective, scalable workforce training worldwide. Read this case study to learn how they empower learners with essential skills for job readiness and career growth.

body.text: Generation: You Employed is a global nonprofit committed to helping adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Established in 2015, Generation operates in 17 countries, partnering with governments, employers, and others to provide adult learners with the skills needed for meaningful careers. With over 122,000 graduates and 18,000 employer partners across 46 professions, Generation equips learners for success in otherwise inaccessible jobs. In addition to training and placement, Generation conducts original research and shares data insights on global workforce transitions to inform decision-making and enhance the employment ecosystem.

In addition to training and placement, Generation conducts original research and shares data insights on global workforce transitions to inform decision-making and enhance the employment ecosystem.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: As Generation moved to embrace online learning, they faced the challenge of scaling their curriculum globally while navigating diverse technical environments, from high-speed urban areas to low-tech rural regions. To address this, they looked for a learning management system (LMS) that would seamlessly deliver their programs under various conditions and scale alongside their program’s growth. Additionally, the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the demand for online learning solutions. Generation needed a platform that could rapidly transition to fully remote delivery without sacrificing learner engagement or the quality of their curriculum while achieving their primary goal – ensuring that every learner, whether in a high-tech city or a remote village, had equal access to highquality education.

title: Badges Become Degrees at British Columbia Institute of Technology
snippet: British Columbia Institute of Technology meets the needs of today’s students
intro: British Columbia Institute of Technology meets the needs of today’s students while adapting to the changing employment needs of industries across British Columbia. Learn how Parchment Digital Badges help make it happen.

body.heading: The challenge
body.text: Learning today calls for tailored classes and programs that students can apply to a specific job skill and need, whether they’re just beginning their careers or are updating their capabilities to meet the changing market. British Columbia Institute of Technology has a strong history of working with industry partners to prepare students for the careers in demand throughout the region. Using short, for-credit credentialing is a mainstay of its education programs. Wanting to further align its offerings with the skill sets that students and industry were looking for, the institution began a laddered approach in 2021 to align its badged courses, microcredential programs, flexible, part-time learning, and full-time education programs with industry needs. The goal was to provide an easy-to-follow and clear educational journey for students. BCIT saw how digital credentialing offers students a way to stand out among their peers, and helps differentiate the institution from others. Additionally, implementing their credentialing system in a way that would help maintain compliance with Canadian information privacy requirements was critically important. Following its search, BCIT selected Parchment Digital Badges (formerly known as Canvas Credentials) for its digital badging needs

Eric FryAssociate Dean of Agile and Work Integrated Learning, BCIT

body.heading: Putting microcredentialing to the test
body.text: With a short timeline for implementation, the BCIT team moved forward with a robust pilot program, evaluating three distinct delivery models for microcredentialing. The first model provided a variety of individual, competency-based courses for students to choose from, such as networking foundations, YouTube marketing, and ECommerce. Courses ranged from .5 to 3 credit hours each. Students completing four course badges received a Digital Transformation microcredential certificate. With the second model, BCIT partnered with Vancouver Island University to offer courses on natural resource and environmental protection, with each institution offering a badge for completed courses. Students completing both sets of courses were issued a microcredential.

body.text: Badging within the legal requirements of its province served up some initial challenges for BCIT. body.text: As a testament to its success, BCIT students now have more than 250 course badges and nearly 80 program microcredentials to choose from. Students completing their coursework have easy access to their badges and certificates, which they can load into their digital backpack, share on social media, or print as a verifiable parchment. Instant verification to potential employers helps demonstrate that students’ skills-based learning is preparing them to fulfill the roles that they are applying for. “Microcredentials help show employers what students can do. Badges are labeled logically, showing for example, that a student knows how to fly a drone, or knows the essentials of network security, or knows how to do stenography,” said Eric. “There’s security built into it, with metadata that shows when you took the course, when the credential expires, and how students were evaluated. title: Alabama Community College System: A Canvas Customer Spotlight
snippet: Learn why ACCS implemented a statewide migration of Canvas LMS.
intro: Learn why ACCS implemented a statewide migration of Canvas LMS.

body.text: Canvas LMS Alabama Community College System A Canvas Customer Spotlight The Alabama Community College System (opens in a new tab) (ACCS) consists of 24 community and technical colleges across the state of Alabama, and includes the Alabama Technology Network and Marion Military Institute – one of only five junior military colleges in the nation. With hundreds of thousands of high school students and adult learners choosing the system’s colleges each year, the ACCS desired a unified LMS to eliminate barriers that hinder seamless student experiences. In 2021, ACCS expanded its usage of Canvas learning management system (LMS) to 12 member institutions and in 2024 implemented a statewide deployment of Instructure Learning Platform solutions that include Canvas LMS, Canvas Studio, Impact by Instructure and Canvas Credentials. body.text: The LA County Department of Public Health (Public Health) is committed to advancing the conditions that support optimal health and well-being for all. Faced with an increase in Community Health Workers (CHW), it developed a comprehensive training tailored for internal staff and external stakeholders, focusing on clear communication and accessible, flexible learning options. This effort aimed to improve process efficiency and content accessibility, allowing for realtime updates and self-paced learning in a dynamic environment.

body.text: Public Health faced challenges with the complexity and inefficiency of its previous system, which involved leveraging internal systems that were not designed for external access. This highlighted the need for a more user-friendly and centralized solution like Canvas LMS.

title: Kinesio Group Scales Global Education with Canvas LMS
snippet: Discover how Kinesio Group leveraged Canvas LMS to scale global education
intro: Discover how Kinesio Group leveraged Canvas LMS to scale global education, enhance learner engagement, and streamline course delivery for students worldwide. Read the full case study to learn more about their success.

body.text: Kinesio Group, a renowned organization comprising Kinesio University, KHC, KTAI, and Cre-Med, has pioneered the elastic therapeutic taping industry. Founded by Dr. Kenzo Kase in the 1970s, the group has a rich legacy of developing and promoting kinesio tape, which is now widely used globally for therapeutic and rehabilitative purposes. Kinesio University is dedicated to training practitioners worldwide, ensuring that instructors and certified Kinesio Taping Practitioners (CKTP) are well-equipped to utilize and teach this innovative method.
body.html: Kinesio Group, a renowned organization comprising Kinesio University, KHC, KTAI, and Cre-Med, has pioneered the elastic therapeutic taping industry. Founded by Dr. Kenzo Kase in the 1970s, the group has a rich legacy of developing and promoting kinesio tape, which is now widely used globally for therapeutic and rehabilitative purposes. Kinesio University is dedicated to training practitioners worldwide, ensuring that instructors and certified Kinesio Taping Practitioners (CKTP) are well-equipped to utilize and teach this innovative method.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: As a global organization with instructors and learners spread over 100 countries, Kinesio University faced challenges delivering consistent, up-to-date education and maintaining a strong sense of community. Instructors relied on PowerPoint presentations and physical workbooks, making it challenging to ensure everyone had access to the most up-to-date materials. This manual approach often resulted in discrepancies and inefficiencies, as there was no centralized system to track and update course materials or maintain ongoing relationships with students post-training. Additionally, maintaining engagement and fostering ongoing relationships with students post-training posed significant difficulties without a centralized system in place.

This manual approach often resulted in discrepancies and inefficiencies, as there was no centralized system to track and update course materials or maintain ongoing relationships with students post-training. body.heading: Key Insights
body.text: Before Canvas, Kinesio University struggled with the inconsistent distribution of training materials globally, relying on manual methods like PowerPoint and workbooks. Since adopting Canvas, Kinesio University has improved resource accessibility and strengthened instructor-learner relationships. By leveraging Canvas's intuitive interface and collaborative features, Kinesio University continues to uphold its legacy of innovation and excellence in global health improvement.

body.heading: The Solution
body.text: After evaluating several options, Kinesio University chose Canvas as its learning management system (LMS). body.text: With Canvas, we can keep the education in one location, make sure everyone's teaching the same, and then keep ongoing relationships with our learners.
body.html:
With Canvas, we can keep the education in one location, make sure everyone's teaching the same, and then keep ongoing relationships with our learners.

Danielle Sanchez,Kinesio University Lead/Project Coordinator, Kinesio University

body.heading: Educational Consistency And Quality
body.text: One of the major challenges Kinesio University previously faced was ensuring all instructors were teaching from the latest, approved educational materials and methods. With instructors relying on PowerPoint presentations and workbooks, it was difficult to control version consistency. By centralizing their curricula on the Canvas LMS, Kinesio can now easily update course materials in one place, providing instant access to the newest versions across all regions. "Once we changed [the education], we wouldn't have to remember to make sure everybody got it. It was something that was automatically done,” explained Danielle Sanchez, Kinesio University Lead/Project Coordinator. The templates and tools within Canvas also allow their education team to build highly structured, visual, and interactive courses that go beyond static presentations. "Canvas is very visual," noted Mona Angel, Director of Business Operations. "That was one of the things we liked - it was kind of intuitive how you move around." Features like integrated quizzing enable Kinesio University to incorporate comprehension checks and assessments into the courses directly. This promotes an active, engaging learning experience and ensures students grasp core taping concepts before moving on.

title: Data-Driven Instructional Growth at De Soto 73
snippet: Better assessments provided the united instructional roadmap De Soto 73 needed
intro: Better assessments provided the united instructional roadmap De Soto 73 needed to move the needle on student achievement.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: De Soto School District needed a strategy to boost student achievement. Teachers worked diligently to support their students, but assessments posed a significant obstacle. Creating them was time-consuming; formats varied widely, and aligning them to standards proved difficult. Elementary teacher Maddy Overmann and High School teachers Lindsey Brinkman and Erin Beck weighed in on the challenges. "Many times, these assessments were not as aligned with the standards as they could have been and were harder to grade," said Overmann. "I was using paper or Google Forms and spending up to three days on a single test." A fragmented assessment approach made meaningful data analysis extremely challenging. "We struggled to prepare students for state tests," recalled Brinkman. "It was hard to get specific insights into student mastery from the data we had," added Beck. When Ron Farrow joined as Assistant Superintendent in 2021, he recognized the need for unified assessment anchored in learning standards. "We needed to go back to basics by putting standards at the center and providing accessible data to drive instructional decisions," Farrow explained.

De Soto School District needed a strategy to boost student achievement. Teachers worked diligently to support their students, but assessments posed a significant obstacle. Creating them was time-consuming; formats varied widely, and aligning them to standards proved difficult. Elementary teacher Maddy Overmann and High School teachers Lindsey Brinkman and Erin Beck weighed in on the challenges.

"Many times, these assessments were not as aligned with the standards as they could have been and were harder to grade," said Overmann. "I was using paper or Google Forms and spending up to three days on a single test."

A fragmented assessment approach made meaningful data analysis extremely challenging. "We struggled to prepare students for state tests," recalled Brinkman. "It was hard to get specific insights into student mastery from the data we had," added Beck.

When Ron Farrow joined as Assistant Superintendent in 2021, he recognized the need for unified assessment anchored in learning standards.

"We needed to go back to basics by putting standards at the center and providing accessible data to drive instructional decisions," Farrow explained.

body.heading: Key Insights
body.text: Generic tests provided shallow, unhelpful data. Teachers needed assessments closely tied to standards. Unified assessments paired with standards-unpacking work enabled data-driven teaching. Since implementing Mastery Connect, De Soto has seen more meaningful assessments and double-digit growth in core subjects.

• Generic tests provided shallow, unhelpful data.

  • Unified assessments paired with standards-unpacking work enabled data-driven teaching.
  • Since implementing Mastery Connect, De Soto has seen more meaningful assessments and double-digit growth in core subjects.

body.heading: The solution
body.text: De Soto adopted Mastery Connect as their assessment management system, drawn to its user-friendly features and ability to align assessments to standards deeply. Through intuitive assessment-building tools, teachers could finally craft high-quality common assessments collectively. "Mastery Connect was brought in as a tool. We are doing standards-unpacking work within it. It gave us a great opportunity to rewrite our assessments to focus on true rigor and depth,” Farrow said.
body.html:
De Soto adopted Mastery Connect as their assessment management system, drawn to its user-friendly features and ability to align assessments to standards deeply. Through intuitive assessment-building tools, teachers could finally craft high-quality common assessments collectively.

"Mastery Connect was brought in as a tool. We are doing standards-unpacking work within it. It gave us a great opportunity to rewrite our assessments to focus on true rigor and depth,” Farrow said.

body.heading: Meeting students where they are
body.text: “We always say that we want to focus on assessment for learning rather than just assessment of learning,” Brinkman said. Over the summer ahead of implementation, teachers underwent training on building valid assessments through Mastery Connect. Change was hard, but the opportunity to unpack standards, re-work questions, and write custom items was invaluable. "When we got Mastery Connect, we were excited to go through and match every question to standards. It made us look at item specs and unpack the standards," Overmann said. "We were nervous about creating tests at first, but Mastery Connect made us examine what's hitting the standards and what's not." De Soto facilitated PD on the "why" behind common assessments to drive teacher buy-in. As teachers saw their new assessments yield more precise mastery data, buy-in increased. The visually-driven reports made digesting results easy. "The data visualization was a huge draw - it allowed us to finally get instructionally-relevant insights we were missing,” Farrow explained. The assessments also provided a wide range of opportunities for students to showcase learning. "Mastery Connect has been good about varying depth of knowledge, showing where students are. It gives us the best of both worlds - measuring skills and applied critical thinking,” Brinkman said. "We were able to shorten tests quite a bit and make them more meaningful while also getting quicker feedback," noted Ms. Overmann. "It helped us take out questions that didn't align well and narrow down what we truly needed to teach."

snippet: Learn how Collin College stores and secures student data.
intro: Learn how Collin College stores and secures student data.

body.text: Collin College , located in McKinney, Texas, is a prominent public community college known for its commitment to academic excellence and student success. Established in 1985, the college has become a cornerstone of the region's educational landscape, offering a wide array of programs and courses. With a focus on innovation and community engagement, Collin College began using Canvas LMS in 2016 to further provide a supportive learning environment for more than 58,800 credit and noncredit students. Both faculty and students enjoy the platform and its easy usability, adding more than 85,000 courses to Canvas by 2023. This rapid growth presented a new challenge for the college: managing and archiving the increasing number of courses on the platform.

Collin College, located in McKinney, Texas, is a prominent public community college known for its commitment to academic excellence and student success. Established in 1985, the college has become a cornerstone of the region's educational landscape, offering a wide array of programs and courses.

With a focus on innovation and community engagement, Collin College began using Canvas LMS in 2016 to further provide a supportive learning environment for more than 58,800 credit and noncredit students.

Both faculty and students enjoy the platform and its easy usability, adding more than 85,000 courses to Canvas by 2023. This rapid growth presented a new challenge for the college: managing and archiving the increasing number of courses on the platform.

body.heading: Key Insights
body.text: Having added more than 85,000 to Canvas since migrating to the LMS in 2016, Collin College set out to find an archiving solution. The college wanted a solution that would allow them to maintain access to existing courses and provide additional storage – all while keeping data accurate and secure. Using Canvas Archiving powered by K16 Solutions, Collin College migrated three years of student data and can now securely store both course content and student data that seamlessly integrates with Canvas LMS.
body.html:
• Having added more than 85,000 to Canvas since migrating to the LMS in 2016, Collin College set out to find an archiving solution.
  • The college wanted a solution that would allow them to maintain access to existing courses and provide additional storage – all while keeping data accurate and secure.
  • Using Canvas Archiving powered by K16 Solutions, Collin College migrated three years of student data and can now securely store both course content and student data that seamlessly integrates with Canvas LMS.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: Limited space Collin College needed to archive courses because it was nearing the individual storage limit of Canvas's LMS platform. Student storage space was a major concern as students cannot upload more assignments once it’s full. The growing volume of coursework also made it difficult for faculty to find what they needed, resulting in longer load times and a more time-consuming search process. Security risks With federal laws like the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and potential regulations similar to the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation on the horizon, the team at Collin College wanted to stay ahead of the game in terms of security. They also wanted to provide grade information to the right users without worrying about sensitive student information being at risk. However, there was no streamlined method to achieve this. Team members were tasked with manually hiding sensitive information for each student, which was time-consuming and prone to errors. Academic integrity concerns Maintaining some level of historical LMS data is crucial for upholding state requirements. It provides a record of past courses, assignments, and grades, which can be crucial for verifying student grades and resolving disputes. Deleting older content would make pulling that data impossible and could jeopardize the college's academic integrity.

body.text: MINDS-i Education is an innovative venture driven by a passion for advancing STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) education, particularly in robotics and technology. The latest addition, an autonomous farming tractor, showcases MINDS-i Education's commitment to pushing the boundaries of learning.

intro: Canvas LMS has revolutionized member education for USA Swimming, providing a centralized platform for comprehensive learning accessible to over 20,000 coaches nationwide. By leveraging Canvas's flexibility, the organization offers interactive content and hybrid courses, catering to diverse learning styles and preferences. Read the full case study to learn more.

body.text: USA Swimming serves as the national governing body for the sport of swimming within the United States. Despite its prominent role in shaping Olympic dreams, USA Swimming's core mission lies in supporting local swim programs, nurturing talent, and instilling life skills in young athletes. With a vast network of clubs and hundreds of thousands of members, USA Swimming recognizes the pivotal role coaches and officials play in the sport's success and seeks to provide them with comprehensive support and education.
body.html: USA Swimming serves as the national governing body for the sport of swimming within the United States. Despite its prominent role in shaping Olympic dreams, USA Swimming's core mission lies in supporting local swim programs, nurturing talent, and instilling life skills in young athletes. With a vast network of clubs and hundreds of thousands of members, USA Swimming recognizes the pivotal role coaches and officials play in the sport's success and seeks to provide them with comprehensive support and education.

body.heading: Key Insights
body.text: Before adopting Canvas LMS, USA Swimming lacked a centralized platform for coach education, resulting in fragmented resources and inconsistent learning. Canvas transformed coach education by providing access to comprehensive content accessible anytime, anywhere. USA Swimming is dedicated to using Canvas to enhance coach education, continually fostering growth and excellence in the sport.
body.html:
• Before adopting Canvas LMS, USA Swimming lacked a centralized platform for coach education, resulting in fragmented resources and inconsistent learning.
  • Canvas transformed coach education by providing access to comprehensive content accessible anytime, anywhere.
  • USA Swimming is dedicated to using Canvas to enhance coach education, continually fostering growth and excellence in the sport.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: Despite reaching a large audience, USA Swimming faced a big challenge: providing comprehensive education and support to its widespread membership, mainly its 20,000 coaches. They knew coaches played a crucial role in shaping athletes' experiences but needed help offering consistent learning opportunities. “We had never taken ownership of the education of our coaches, and our board of directors wanted to provide education to our membership because they can make or break the experience for a kid in sports,” said Maggie Vail, Program Director, Education & Curriculum. “We had a team of subject matter experts work on curriculum and then asked ourselves how we get this to people.” The organization recognized the need for a centralized platform to deliver high-quality educational content and resources to coaches across the country. The answer? Canvas LMS.
body.html:
Despite reaching a large audience, USA Swimming faced a big challenge: providing comprehensive education and support to its widespread membership, mainly its 20,000 coaches. They knew coaches played a crucial role in shaping athletes' experiences but needed help offering consistent learning opportunities.

“We had never taken ownership of the education of our coaches, and our board of directors wanted to provide education to our membership because they can make or break the experience for a kid in sports,” said Maggie Vail, Program Director, Education & Curriculum. “We had a team of subject matter experts work on curriculum and then asked ourselves how we get this to people.”

The organization recognized the need for a centralized platform to deliver high-quality educational content and resources to coaches across the country. The answer? Canvas LMS.

body.heading: The Solution
body.text: To address the challenge of providing support to its diverse learning population, spanning from junior coaches to seasoned professionals, USA Swimming turned to Canvas LMS. This centralized platform streamlined access to highquality educational content, catering to learners of all ages and experience levels. “We did a lot of research into different LMS solutions. There were very few options that checked all of the boxes, or even most of them,” said Vail. “That’s what brought Canvas to the top of our list.“ By leveraging Canvas LMS, USA Swimming effectively addressed the needs of different age groups to online learning, providing a scalable and intuitive platform for delivering educational resources and fostering continuous improvement among coaches.

body.text: Our internal IT department had encouraged us to consider custom development, but Canvas solved many of our needs without requiring it.

Maggie VailProgram Director, Education & Curriculum, USA Swimming

body.heading: Supporting Online Learning For All Ages
body.text: USA Swimming's initial concerns about the adaptability of different age groups to online learning were quickly alleviated when they discovered the widespread familiarity with Canvas among users. Moreover, they were pleasantly surprised to find a demand for more interactive content, such as quizzes and challenges, to enrich the learning experience. This unexpected feedback prompted USA Swimming to pivot its learning design strategy, focusing on asynchronous activities that effectively engage users. “Just how widespread Canvas is in the market has worked in our favor,” said Vail. With Canvas LMS, USA Swimming can confidently address its members' diverse needs, regardless of age, better supporting their transition to online learning and providing an enriching educational experience that fosters skill development and personal growth.

body.heading: Course Mix - Certs, Hybrids, And More!
body.text: USA Swimming has developed various courses over the past few years, including certifications for coaches and officials. These courses feature video-based content, quizzes, and other interactive elements. While they primarily focus on certifications, there are also shorter courses for continuing education. They are piloting hybrid courses combining online learning with in-person coaching clinics and plan to expand their offerings based on user feedback, potentially including topics like open-water swimming and nutrition.

title: Clemson University: Creating Better Student Outcomes with Canvas LMS and Praxis AI
snippet: Learn how Clemson University provides 24/7 educational support for students.
intro: Learn how Clemson University provides 24/7 educational support for students.

body.text: Educators today are tasked with instructional design, teaching, research, and a myriad of other tasks related to teaching and learning that can unintentionally leave students feeling unsupported. Understanding the need to bridge this teaching-learning gap, a Clemson University professor found a way to provide students with 24-7 access to educational support. How? Generative AI. By integrating Pria, a generative AI teaching assistant, into the Canvas learning management system (LMS), Clemson educators can give students around-theclock access to trusted educational support, freeing up more time to focus on pedagogy and student learning outcomes.
body.html:
Educators today are tasked with instructional design, teaching, research, and a myriad of other tasks related to teaching and learning that can unintentionally leave students feeling unsupported. Understanding the need to bridge this teaching-learning gap, a Clemson University professor found a way to provide students with 24-7 access to educational support. How? Generative AI.

By integrating Pria, a generative AI teaching assistant, into the Canvas learning management system (LMS), Clemson educators can give students around-theclock access to trusted educational support, freeing up more time to focus on pedagogy and student learning outcomes.

body.heading: The Challenge
body.text: As one of the most productive public research universities in the nation, Clemson University focuses on preparing our students, educators, and researchers for global challenges like artificial intelligence. While its use inside and outside the classroom has the ability to save educators and students time, concerns around data privacy and the overall efficacy of AI tools make it challenging for the Clemson community to test the AI waters. Generative AI tools like Chat GPT can pose significant risks as they rely on large language models that provide limited control over generated content, are inherently biased, can spread misinformation and hallucinate, lack emotional intelligence, and raise privacy and security concerns.

body.heading: Key Insights
body.text: Seeking a safe way to introduce AI to Clemson University students, Professor Alex Feltus found a way to provide 24/7 educational support to the university’s students and educators. By integrating the AI teaching assistant Pria (developed by Praxis AI) into Canvas LMS, students can enter prompts and retrieve cited answers from 28 trusted sources – addressing the privacy and data concerns many educators have regarding AI. Using Canvas and Pria in his courses, Dr. Feltus found that the AI tool created a safe, alwaysaccessible space for students to ask questions and learn. This seamless integration allows Clemson University educators to give students around-the-clock access to trusted educational support, and free up more time to focus on student learning outcomes.

body.heading: The Solution
body.text: In learning about and experimenting with Pria in his Canvas courses and research, Professor Alex Feltus at Clemson University, realized that while this tool is designed with the same concept as ChatGPT – utilizing prompts – it’s different. Unlike most existing AI tools, Pria retrieves its answers from 28 trusted sources, provides citations for the information’s source, does not hallucinate, and integrates seamlessly with Canvas LMS.
